\begin{definitionv}{synth_2}[Joint multinomial covariance]
Fix \(p\in(0,1)\) and \(\mathcal M\in\mathfrak M_{+}\). Let \(T_{x,y}=(\operatorname{vec}H_x,z_{x,y},b)\), and let \(\widehat T_{x,y,n}=(\operatorname{vec}\widehat H_{x,n},\widehat z_{x,y,n},\widehat b_n)\) be formed from independent source and target samples with \(n_s(n)/n\to p\) and \(n_t(n)/n\to1-p\). Define \(\Gamma_{x,y}(\mathcal M;p)\) to be the covariance matrix of the centered Gaussian limit of \(\sqrt n(\widehat T_{x,y,n}-T_{x,y})\). Equivalently, its source block is \(p^{-1}\) times the multinomial covariance of the source cell indicators defining \(H_x\) and \(z_{x,y}\) under \(P_O\), its target block is \((1-p)^{-1}\) times the multinomial covariance of the target proxy indicators defining \(b\), and the source--target cross blocks are zero.
\end{definitionv}

\begin{assumptionv}{ass:latent-shift-factorization}[Latent-shift factorization]
For every source cell \((e,u,w,x,y)\),
\[
P_{\mathcal M}(e,u,w,x,y)
=
\pi_e S_{ue} M_{wu} a_x(u) f_{x,y}(u,w).
\]
\end{assumptionv}

\begin{assumptionv}{ass:target-mechanism-invariance}[Target mechanism invariance]
For every target cell \((u,w,x,y)\),
\[
Q_{\mathcal M}(u,w,x,y)
=
q_u M_{wu} a_x(u) f_{x,y}(u,w).
\]
\end{assumptionv}

\begin{assumptionv}{ass:strict-primitive-positivity}[Strict primitive positivity]
Every entry of \(\pi\), \(S\), \(M\), \(a\), \(f\), and \(q\) is strictly positive.
\end{assumptionv}

\begin{assumptionv}{ass:proxy-channel-injectivity}[Proxy-channel injectivity]
The proxy channel \(M\) has full column rank:
\[
\operatorname{rank}(M)=r.
\]
\end{assumptionv}

\begin{definitionv}{synth_3}[Finite latent-shift state spaces]
The latent-shift state spaces are finite sets \(\mathcal E,\mathcal U,\mathcal W,\mathcal X,\mathcal Y\), where \(\mathcal E\) is the source-environment state space and \(\mathcal X\) is the treatment state space, both nonempty. The latent state space \(\mathcal U\) has cardinality \(r=\lvert\mathcal U\rvert\) with \(2\le r\). The proxy state space \(\mathcal W\) has cardinality \(m=\lvert\mathcal W\rvert\) with \(m\ge r\). The outcome state space \(\mathcal Y\) satisfies \(\lvert\mathcal Y\rvert\ge2\).
\end{definitionv}

\begin{assumptionv}{ass:source-iid-sampling}[Source iid sampling]
The observed source marginal law \(P_O\) induced by \(P_{\mathcal M}\) is defined by
\[
P_O(e,w,x,y)
=
\sum_{u\in\mathcal U}
P_{\mathcal M}(E=e,U=u,W=w,X=x,Y=y).
\]
The source observations \(O_1^s,\ldots,O_{n_s}^s\) are independent and identically distributed according to \(P_O\).
\end{assumptionv}

\begin{assumptionv}{ass:target-iid-sampling}[Target-proxy iid sampling]
The target proxy marginal vector \(b\) induced by \(\mathcal M\) is defined by
\[
b(w)=\sum_{u\in\mathcal U} M(w\mid u)\,q(u),
\qquad w\in\mathcal W.
\]
Under the sampling law on \(\Omega(n_s,n_t)\), the target-proxy block \((W_1^t,\ldots,W_{n_t}^t)\) has product law \(\bigotimes_{j=1}^{n_t} b\).
\end{assumptionv}

\begin{assumptionv}{ass:triangular-allocation}[Triangular allocation]
The source sample size \(n_s(n)\) and target-proxy sample size \(n_t(n)\) form a fixed deterministic sequence \(\{(n_s(n),n_t(n))\}_{n\ge 2}\) such that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Positive row sizes.)} \((n_s(n),n_t(n))\in\mathbb N_{\ge 1}^{2}\) for every \(n\ge 2\).
\item \textbf{(Row total.)} \(n_s(n)+n_t(n)=n\) for every \(n\ge 2\).
\item \textbf{(Source allocation limit.)} \(n_s(n)/n\to p\in(0,1)\) as \(n\to\infty\).
\end{itemize}
\end{assumptionv}

\begin{definitionv}{synth_4}[Normalized finite latent-shift SCM]
A normalized finite latent-shift SCM on finite state spaces \(\mathcal E,\mathcal U,\mathcal W,\mathcal X,\mathcal Y\) is a tuple \(\mathcal M=(\pi,S,M,a,f,q)\) Markov relative to the graph with arrows \(E\to U\), \(U\to W\), \(U\to X\), \(U\to Y\), \(W\to Y\), and \(X\to Y\). The primitive \(\pi\in\Delta^{\circ}(\mathcal E)\) is a strictly positive environment law; \(S\in\mathbb R^{r\times\lvert\mathcal E\rvert}\) is a strictly positive column-stochastic latent channel with \(S_{ue}=P(U=u\mid E=e)\); \(M\in\mathbb R^{m\times r}\) is a strictly positive column-stochastic proxy channel with \(M_{wu}=P(W=w\mid U=u)\); \(a\) is a strictly positive treatment kernel with \(a_x(u)=P(X=x\mid U=u)\); \(f\) is a strictly positive outcome kernel with \(f_{x,y}(u,w)=P(Y=y\mid U=u,W=w,X=x)\); and \(q\in\Delta^{\circ}(\mathcal U)\) is a strictly positive target latent mixture with \(q_u=Q(U=u)\). Normalization means \(\sum_e\pi_e=1\), \(\sum_u S_{ue}=1\) for each \(e\), \(\sum_w M_{wu}=1\) for each \(u\), \(\sum_x a_x(u)=1\) for each \(u\), \(\sum_y f_{x,y}(u,w)=1\) for each \((u,w,x)\), and \(\sum_u q_u=1\). The SCM induces the source full-data law \(P_{\mathcal M}\) on \(\mathcal E\times\mathcal U\times\mathcal W\times\mathcal X\times\mathcal Y\) with cell probabilities \(P_{\mathcal M}(e,u,w,x,y)=\pi_e S_{ue}M_{wu}a_x(u)f_{x,y}(u,w)\), and the target law \(Q_{\mathcal M}\) on \(\mathcal U\times\mathcal W\times\mathcal X\times\mathcal Y\) with cell probabilities \(Q_{\mathcal M}(u,w,x,y)=q_uM_{wu}a_x(u)f_{x,y}(u,w)\).
\end{definitionv}

\begin{assumptionv}{ass:triangular-source-iid-sampling}[Triangular source sampling]
The row models \((\mathcal M_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}\) are normalized finite latent-shift SCMs on the finite state spaces \(\mathcal E,\mathcal U,\mathcal W,\mathcal X,\mathcal Y\). For row \(n\), the observed source law \(P_{O,n}\) is defined by
\[
P_{O,n}(e,w,x,y)
=
\sum_{u\in\mathcal U}
P_{\mathcal M_n}(E=e,U=u,W=w,X=x,Y=y),
\]
and, writing \(M_n\) for the row proxy channel and \(q_n\) for the row target latent-state probability mass function, the target proxy law \(b_n\) is defined by
\[
b_n(w)=\sum_{u\in\mathcal U} M_n(w,u)q_n(u),
\qquad w\in\mathcal W.
\]
For sample sizes \(n_s,n_t\), the finite two-sample product sample space, with its discrete full power-set sigma-field, is
\[
\Omega(n_s,n_t)
=
(\mathcal E\times\mathcal W\times\mathcal X\times\mathcal Y)^{n_s}
\times
\mathcal W^{n_t},
\]
with
\[
\Omega_n=\Omega(n_s(n),n_t(n)).
\]
For every \(n\ge 2\), the finite row law on \(\Omega_n\) is
\[
\mathbb P_{\mathcal M_n}^{\,n_s(n),n_t(n)}
=
P_{O,n}^{\otimes n_s(n)}\otimes b_n^{\otimes n_t(n)}.
\]
The source observations \((O^s_{1,n},\ldots,O^s_{n_s(n),n})\) are the source coordinate block under this law, and their marginal law is
\[
(\mathbb P_{\mathcal M_n}^{\,n_s(n),n_t(n)})\circ
(O^s_{1,n},\ldots,O^s_{n_s(n),n})^{-1}
=
P_{O,n}^{\otimes n_s(n)}.
\]
\end{assumptionv}

\begin{assumptionv}{ass:triangular-target-iid-sampling}[Target-proxy row sampling]
For every \(n\ge 2\), the target proxy observations \((W^t_{1,n},\ldots,W^t_{n_t(n),n})\) are the target coordinate block under the finite row law
\[
\mathbb P_{\mathcal M_n}^{\,n_s(n),n_t(n)}
=
P_{O,n}^{\otimes n_s(n)}\otimes b_n^{\otimes n_t(n)}
\]
on \(\Omega_n\).
\end{assumptionv}

\begin{assumptionv}{ass:array-target-span}[Row-wise target span]
For each \(n\), let \(B_{x,n}\) denote the row-\(n\) conditional proxy matrix with entries
\[
B_{x,n}(e,w)=P_{O,n}(W=w\mid E=e,X=x),
\qquad e\in\mathcal E,\ w\in\mathcal W .
\]
The row-\(n\) target proxy law \(b_n\) satisfies
\[
b_n\in\operatorname{col}(B_{x,n}).
\]
\end{assumptionv}

\begin{assumptionv}{ass:regular-fixed-rank}[Fixed source rank]
The fixed source moment matrix \(H_x\) satisfies
\[
\operatorname{rank}(H_x)=r_0.
\]
\end{assumptionv}

\begin{assumptionv}{ass:regular-singular-gap}[Retained singular gap]
The retained singular value satisfies
\[
\sigma_{r_0}(H_x)\ge c.
\]
\end{assumptionv}

\begin{assumptionv}{ass:regular-target-span}[Regular target span]
The fixed target proxy vector lies in the column space of the source moment matrix:
\[
b\in\operatorname{col}(H_x).
\]
\end{assumptionv}

\begin{assumptionv}{ass:regular-cell-floor}[Regular cell floor]
The source observed cells and target proxy cells have common lower bound \(\eta\):
\[
\min\bigl(\{P_O(e,w,x,y):e\in\mathcal E,\ w\in\mathcal W,\ x\in\mathcal X,\ y\in\mathcal Y\}\cup\{b_w:w\in\mathcal W\}\bigr)\ge\eta.
\]
\end{assumptionv}

\begin{assumptionv}{ass:regular-positive-variance}[Positive Wald variance]
Let \(V_{r_0,x,y}(\mathcal M;p)\) denote the population delta-method variance of the retained-rank Wald functional \(\phi_{r_0}\) at the population moment tuple \((H_x,z_{x,y},b)\), with source allocation limit \(p\) and target-proxy allocation limit \(1-p\). It satisfies
\[
V_{r_0,x,y}(\mathcal M;p)\ge\eta .
\]
\end{assumptionv}

\begin{definitionv}{def:positive-latent-shift-class}[Strictly positive latent-shift class \(\mathfrak M_{+}\)]
\[
\mathfrak M_{+}
=
\{\mathcal M=(\pi,S,M,a,f,q):
\mathcal M \text{ satisfies } \cref{obj:ass:latent-shift-factorization,obj:ass:target-mechanism-invariance,obj:ass:strict-primitive-positivity}
\text{ and } \operatorname{rank}(M)=r\}.
\]
Here \(r=\lvert\mathcal U\rvert\), the latent cardinality, and the full-column-rank proxy condition is the one in \cref{obj:ass:proxy-channel-injectivity}.
\end{definitionv}

\begin{definitionv}{def:compatible-fiber}[Compatible SCM fiber \(\mathfrak F(\mathcal D)\)]
\[
\mathfrak F(\mathcal D)
=
\{\mathcal M\in\mathfrak M_{+}:
\mathcal M \text{ induces exactly the supplied } P_O \text{ and } b\}.
\]
\end{definitionv}

\begin{definitionv}{def:balancing-fiber}[Balancing fiber \(\Lambda_x(\mathcal D)\)]
\[
\Lambda_x(\mathcal D)
=
\{\lambda\in\mathbb R^{\lvert\mathcal E\rvert}:B_x\lambda=b\}.
\]
\end{definitionv}

\begin{definitionv}{def:failure-separator}[Failure separators \(\mathcal H_x(\mathcal D)\)]
\[
\mathcal H_x(\mathcal D)
=
\{h\in\mathbb R^m: h^{\top}B_x=0,\ h^{\top}b\ne 0\}.
\]
\end{definitionv}

\begin{definitionv}{def:outcome-null-perturbation}[Outcome-null perturbation \(f^{(t)}_{x,y}\)]
For \(\mathcal M\in\mathfrak M_{+}\) as in \cref{obj:def:positive-latent-shift-class}, fix \(h\in\mathcal H_x(\mathcal D)\) as in \cref{obj:def:failure-separator}. Put \(v=M^\top h\), choose \(w_{\star}\in\mathcal W\) and \(y^\circ\ne y\), and define
\[
f^{(t)}_{x,y}(u,w_{\star})
=
f_{x,y}(u,w_{\star})+\frac{t v_u}{M_{w_{\star}u}},
\qquad
f^{(t)}_{x,y^\circ}(u,w_{\star})
=
f_{x,y^\circ}(u,w_{\star})-\frac{t v_u}{M_{w_{\star}u}}.
\]
Every other cell of \(f^{(t)}\) equals the corresponding cell of \(f\).
\end{definitionv}

\begin{definitionv}{def:rank-deficient-success-witness}[Rank-deficient witness \(\mathcal M^{\star}\)]
The SCM \(\mathcal M^{\star}\) is specified by
\[
\mathcal E=\{e_1,e_2\},\qquad
\mathcal U=\mathcal W=\{0,1,2\},\qquad
\mathcal X=\mathcal Y=\{0,1\},
\]
\[
\pi=(1/2,1/2),\qquad
S=
\begin{pmatrix}
9/19 & 1/12\\
2/19 & 2/3\\
8/19 & 1/4
\end{pmatrix},
\]
\[
a_1=(1/10,3/5,1/5)^\top,\qquad
a_0=\mathbf 1-a_1,
\]
with \(M\) having diagonal entries \(4/5\) and off-diagonal entries \(1/10\), and
\[
q=(1197,2436,2204)^\top/5837.
\]
For \(i,j\in\{0,1,2\}\) and \(x\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
f_{x,1}(u_i,w_j)=\frac15+\frac{x}{5}+\frac{i}{20}+\frac{j}{100},
\qquad
f_{x,0}(u_i,w_j)=1-f_{x,1}(u_i,w_j).
\]
\end{definitionv}

\begin{definitionv}{def:unconditional-balancing-moments}[Unconditional moments \(H_x\) and \(z_{x,y}\)]
\[
H_x(w,e)=P_O(E=e,W=w,X=x),
\qquad
z_{x,y}(e)=P_O(E=e,X=x,Y=y).
\]
\end{definitionv}

\begin{definitionv}{def:unconditional-weight-map}[Unconditional weight map \(\kappa\)]
For \(\lambda\in\Lambda_x(\mathcal D)\) as in \cref{obj:def:balancing-fiber}, define
\[
\kappa(e)=\frac{\lambda(e)}{P_O(E=e,X=x)}.
\]
\end{definitionv}

\begin{definitionv}{def:concentration-projection-set}[Projection set \(\widehat C_{x,y,1-\alpha}\)]
Let
\[
L=m\lvert\mathcal E\rvert+\lvert\mathcal E\rvert+m,
\qquad
r_s=\sqrt{\frac{\log(2L/\alpha)}{2n_s}},
\qquad
r_t=\sqrt{\frac{\log(2L/\alpha)}{2n_t}}.
\]
Define
\[
\widehat C_{x,y,1-\alpha}
=
\left\{
\vartheta\in[0,1]:
\exists \kappa\in\mathbb R^{\lvert\mathcal E\rvert}
\text{ such that }
\lVert \widehat H_x\kappa-\widehat b\rVert_{\infty}
\le
r_s\lVert\kappa\rVert_1+r_t
\text{ and }
\left|\widehat z_{x,y}^{\top}\kappa-\vartheta\right|
\le
r_s\lVert\kappa\rVert_1
\right\}.
\]
\end{definitionv}

\begin{definitionv}{def:studentized-array-class}[Studentized array class \(\mathcal A_p\)]
Fix the source allocation limit \(p\in(0,1)\) and a deterministic allocation sequence \((n_s(n),n_t(n))_{n\ge2}\) satisfying \cref{obj:ass:triangular-allocation}. Relative to this sequence, and under \cref{obj:ass:triangular-source-iid-sampling,obj:ass:triangular-target-iid-sampling,obj:ass:array-target-span}, define
\[
d_{x,n}
=
\inf\left\{
\|\lambda\|_2:
\lambda\in\mathbb R^{|\mathcal E|},\ B_{x,n}\lambda=b_n
\right\}.
\]
The fixed-allocation changing-rank array class is
\[
\mathcal A_p
=
\left\{
\mathbb M=(\mathcal M_n)_{n\ge2}:
\begin{array}{l}
\text{for every } n\ge2,\ \mathcal M_n \text{ is a finite latent-shift SCM satisfying source-law factorization,}\
\text{target-mechanism invariance, strict positivity of all primitive probabilities, and proxy-channel column rank } r,\
\mathbb P_{\mathcal M_n}^{\,n_s(n),n_t(n)}
=
P_{O,n}^{\otimes n_s(n)}\otimes b_n^{\otimes n_t(n)}
\text{ on } \Omega_n=\Omega(n_s(n),n_t(n)),\
\text{and } b_n\in\operatorname{col}(B_{x,n})
\end{array}
\right\}.
\]
The class includes arrays with row-wise changes in \(\operatorname{rank}(B_{x,n})\), singular joint multinomial covariance, and divergent balancing-weight norm \(d_{x,n}\).
\end{definitionv}

\begin{definitionv}{def:strongly-identified-submodel}[Strongly identified submodel \(\mathcal R_{r_0,c,\eta}\)]
For \(1\le r_0\le\min(m,\lvert\mathcal E\rvert)\) and fixed \(c,\eta>0\), define \(\mathcal R_{r_0,c,\eta}\) as the set of all \(\mathcal M\in\mathfrak M_{+}\) satisfying \cref{obj:def:positive-latent-shift-class,obj:ass:regular-fixed-rank,obj:ass:regular-singular-gap,obj:ass:regular-target-span,obj:ass:regular-cell-floor,obj:ass:regular-positive-variance} through the following conditions:
\[
\mathcal R_{r_0,c,\eta}
=
\left\{
\mathcal M\in\mathfrak M_{+}:
\begin{array}{l}
\operatorname{rank}(H_x)=r_0,\\
\sigma_{r_0}(H_x)\ge c,\\
b\in\operatorname{col}(H_x),\\
\text{every source and target cell is at least }\eta,\\
V_{r_0,x,y}(\mathcal M;p)\ge\eta
\end{array}
\right\}.
\]
\end{definitionv}

\begin{definitionv}{def:regular-wald-functional}[Wald functional \(\phi_{r_0}(H,z,b)\)]
For an integer \(r_0\) satisfying \(1\le r_0\le \min(m,\lvert\mathcal E\rvert)\), \(H\in\mathbb R^{m\times\lvert\mathcal E\rvert}\), \(z\in\mathbb R^{\lvert\mathcal E\rvert}\), and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), define
\[
\phi_{r_0}(H,z,b)=z^{\top}H_{r_0}^{\dagger}b.
\]
Here \(H_{r_0}^{\dagger}\) is the fixed selector-based Gram-spectral truncated pseudoinverse of \(H\): the construction forms the left Gram matrix \(HH^{\top}\), chooses its fixed unitary eigenbasis, inverts exactly the eigenvalues in the first \(r_0\) selected coordinates, sets the remaining diagonal entries to zero, and transports the resulting diagonal inverse back through \(H^{\top}\) and the chosen eigenbasis. The fixed selector determines the value of \(\phi_{r_0}\), including at tied cutoffs.
\end{definitionv}

\begin{definitionv}{def:regular-wald-estimator}[Wald estimator \(\widehat\theta^{\,W}_{x,y,n}\)]
Let \(r_0\) be a regular rank index satisfying
\[
1\le r_0\le \min\{\lvert\mathcal W\rvert,\lvert\mathcal E\rvert\}.
\]
For any supplied row-\(n\) empirical source moment matrix
\(\widehat H_{x,n}\in\mathbb R^{\mathcal W\times\mathcal E}\), row-\(n\) empirical source outcome-moment vector
\(\widehat z_{x,y,n}\in\mathbb R^{\mathcal E}\), and row-\(n\) empirical target proxy vector
\(\widehat b_n\in\mathbb R^{\mathcal W}\), define the truncated-SVD Wald estimator by
\[
\widehat\theta^{\,W}_{x,y,n}
=
\phi_{r_0}(\widehat H_{x,n},\widehat z_{x,y,n},\widehat b_n).
\]
\end{definitionv}

\begin{definitionv}{def:regular-wald-variance}[Wald variance \(\widehat V_n\)]
Put
\[
\widehat T_n=(\widehat H_{x,n},\widehat z_{x,y,n},\widehat b_n).
\]
Let \(\widehat\Gamma_n\) be the plug-in covariance matrix of \(\sqrt n\,\widehat T_n\), formed from the joint source multinomial covariance and the target multinomial covariance with allocation factors \(p^{-1}\) and \((1-p)^{-1}\). Define the totalized plug-in variance by
\[
\widehat V_n=
\begin{cases}
D\phi_{r_0}(\widehat T_n)\,\widehat\Gamma_n\,D\phi_{r_0}(\widehat T_n)^{\top},
&\sigma_{r_0}(\widehat H_{x,n})>\sigma_{r_0+1}(\widehat H_{x,n}),\\
0,&\sigma_{r_0}(\widehat H_{x,n})\le\sigma_{r_0+1}(\widehat H_{x,n}),
\end{cases}
\]
where \(D\phi_{r_0}\) is the ordinary derivative of the selector-independent functional on the strict-cutoff-gap region, and where
\[
\sigma_{\bar q+1}=0,
\qquad
\bar q=\min(m,\lvert\mathcal E\rvert).
\]
The second line is the fixed nonnegative fallback.
\end{definitionv}

\begin{definitionv}{def:regular-wald-interval}[Wald interval \(I^W_{n,1-\alpha}\)]
Let \(z_{1-\alpha/2}\) denote the standard-normal \((1-\alpha/2)\)-quantile. Define the truncated-SVD Wald interval by
\[
I^W_{n,1-\alpha}
=
\left[
\widehat\theta^{\,W}_{x,y,n}
\pm
z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{\widehat V_n/n}
\right]\cap[0,1].
\]
\end{definitionv}

\begin{definitionv}{def:euclidean-diameter}[Euclidean diameter \(\operatorname{diam}_2(C)\)]
For \(C\subseteq[0,1]\), define
\[
\operatorname{diam}_2(C)=\sup_{\xi,\zeta\in C}|\xi-\zeta|,
\]
with the convention \(\operatorname{diam}_2(\varnothing)=0\).
\end{definitionv}

\begin{definitionv}{def:euclidean-hausdorff-distance}[Euclidean Hausdorff distance \(d_H(C,D)\)]
For nonempty \(C,D\subseteq[0,1]\), define the Euclidean Hausdorff distance by
\[
d_H(C,D)=
\max\left\{
\sup_{\xi\in C}\inf_{\zeta\in D}|\xi-\zeta|,
\sup_{\zeta\in D}\inf_{\xi\in C}|\xi-\zeta|
\right\}.
\]
\end{definitionv}

\begin{lemmav}{lem:observable-factorization}[Observable factorization]
Let \(\mathcal M\) be a latent-shift SCM on finite state spaces \(\mathcal E,\mathcal U,\mathcal W,\mathcal X,\mathcal Y\), and suppose that \(\mathcal M\in\mathfrak M_{+}\) in the sense of \cref{obj:def:positive-latent-shift-class}. For \(x\in\mathcal X\), define the source treatment probability and latent posterior matrix by
\[
\rho_x(e)=\sum_{u\in\mathcal U} a_x(u)S(u,e),
\qquad
R_x(u,e)=\frac{a_x(u)S(u,e)}{\rho_x(e)} .
\]
For \(x\in\mathcal X\) and \(y\in\mathcal Y\), define the latent-proxy averaged outcome vector by
\[
g_{x,y}(u)=\sum_{w\in\mathcal W} M(w,u)f_{x,y}(u,w).
\]
Then, for every \(x\in\mathcal X\) and \(y\in\mathcal Y\),
\[
B_x = M R_x,\qquad
b = Mq,\qquad
c_{x,y}=g_{x,y}^{\top}R_x,\qquad
\theta_{x,y}=g_{x,y}^{\top}q .
\]
Moreover, for every \(\lambda\in\Lambda_x(\mathcal D)\), where \(\Lambda_x(\mathcal D)\) is the balancing fiber in \cref{obj:def:balancing-fiber}, the unconditional weight \(\kappa\) induced by \(\lambda\) as in \cref{obj:def:unconditional-weight-map} satisfies
\[
H_x\kappa=b
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
z_{x,y}^{\top}\kappa=\theta_{x,y}.
\]
Finally, there exists a vector \(h:\mathcal W\to\mathbb R\) such that
\[
H_x^{\top}h=z_{x,y}.
\]
\end{lemmav}

\begin{theoremv}{thm:positive-full-law-converse}[Positive full-law converse]
Let \(P_O\) be an observed source law and let \(b\) be a target proxy law. Suppose that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Compatible fiber.)} The compatible fiber \(\mathfrak F(\mathcal D)\) in \cref{obj:def:compatible-fiber}, with \(\mathcal D=(P_O,b)\), is nonempty, and \(\mathcal M\in\mathfrak F(\mathcal D)\).
\item \textbf{(Factorization and invariance.)} The model \(\mathcal M\) satisfies the source-law factorization in \cref{obj:ass:latent-shift-factorization} and the target mechanism invariance condition in \cref{obj:ass:target-mechanism-invariance}.
\item \textbf{(Positivity and proxy rank.)} The model \(\mathcal M\) satisfies strict primitive positivity as in \cref{obj:ass:strict-primitive-positivity}, and its proxy channel has full column rank as in \cref{obj:ass:proxy-channel-injectivity}.
\item \textbf{(Target-span failure.)} For the source conditional proxy matrix \(B_x=P_O(W\mid E,x)\),
\[
B_x\lambda \ne b
\]
for every \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^{\mathcal E}\).
\item \textbf{(Separator and offset cell.)} Fix \(y^\circ\in\mathcal Y\) with \(y^\circ\ne y\), fix \(w_{\star}\in\mathcal W\), and let \(h\in\mathcal H_x(\mathcal D)\), where \(\mathcal H_x(\mathcal D)\) is the failure-separator set in \cref{obj:def:failure-separator}.
\end{itemize}
Then there exists \(\varepsilon>0\) such that, for every \(t\in\mathbb R\) with \(|t|<\varepsilon\), the outcome-null perturbation \(f^{(t)}\) from \cref{obj:def:outcome-null-perturbation}, applied at \((x,y,w_{\star})\) and offset at \(y^\circ\), is nonnegative and sums to one over \(y'\) for every \((x',u,w)\). Let \(\mathcal M_t\) be the latent-shift SCM obtained from \(\mathcal M\) by replacing \(f\) with this \(f^{(t)}\) and recomputing \(P_{\mathcal M_t}\) and \(Q_{\mathcal M_t}\). Then
\[
\mathcal M_t\in\mathfrak F(\mathcal D)
\]
and
\[
\theta_{x,y}(\mathcal M_t)-\theta_{x,y}(\mathcal M)
=
t\,h^\top b .
\]
Consequently, the compatible values of \(\theta_{x,y}\) contain the open interval
\[
\bigl(\theta_{x,y}(\mathcal M)-\varepsilon |h^\top b|,
      \theta_{x,y}(\mathcal M)+\varepsilon |h^\top b|\bigr)
\]
inside the identified interval
\[
\Bigl\{\theta_{x,y}(\widetilde{\mathcal M}):
\widetilde{\mathcal M}\in\mathfrak F(\mathcal D)\Bigr\}.
\]
\end{theoremv}

\begin{theoremv}{thm:target-span-iff}[Target span characterization]
Let \(\mathcal D=(P_O,b)\) be supplied observed and target-proxy data, let \(x\in\mathcal X\) and \(y\in\mathcal Y\), and let \(\mathcal M_0\) be a latent-shift SCM.  Suppose that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Compatible fiber.)} The compatible fiber \(\mathfrak F(\mathcal D)\) of \cref{obj:def:compatible-fiber} is nonempty.
\item \textbf{(Reference model.)} The reference model satisfies \(\mathcal M_0\in\mathfrak F(\mathcal D)\).
\item \textbf{(Proxy injectivity.)} The reference model \(\mathcal M_0\) satisfies the proxy-channel injectivity condition in \cref{obj:ass:proxy-channel-injectivity}.
\end{itemize}
Write
\[
B_x(w,e)=\frac{\sum_{y'\in\mathcal Y}P_O(e,w,x,y')}
{\sum_{w'\in\mathcal W}\sum_{y'\in\mathcal Y}P_O(e,w',x,y')}
\]
for the conditional proxy matrix of \(\mathcal M_0\) at treatment \(x\), and, for each \(\mathcal M\in\mathfrak F(\mathcal D)\), write
\[
c_{x,y}^{\mathcal M}(e)=
\frac{\sum_{w\in\mathcal W}P_O(e,w,x,y)}
{\sum_{w\in\mathcal W}\sum_{y'\in\mathcal Y}P_O(e,w,x,y')}
\]
for its conditional outcome vector at \((x,y)\).  Then the identified interval for the target interventional probability
\[
\theta_{x,y}(\mathcal M)=\sum_{u\in\mathcal U}\sum_{w\in\mathcal W}q_{\mathcal M}(u)M_{\mathcal M}(w,u)f_{\mathcal M,x,y}(u,w)
\]
over \(\mathfrak F(\mathcal D)\) is a singleton if and only if the balancing fiber \(\Lambda_x(\mathcal D)=\{\lambda:B_x\lambda=b\}\) of \cref{obj:def:balancing-fiber} is nonempty.  Moreover, every \(\lambda\in\Lambda_x(\mathcal D)\) satisfies, for every \(\mathcal M\in\mathfrak F(\mathcal D)\),
\[
\theta_{x,y}(\mathcal M)=\sum_{e\in\mathcal E}c_{x,y}^{\mathcal M}(e)\lambda(e).
\]
In particular, for all \(\lambda,\lambda'\in\Lambda_x(\mathcal D)\),
\[
\sum_{e\in\mathcal E}c_{x,y}^{\mathcal M_0}(e)\lambda(e)
=
\sum_{e\in\mathcal E}c_{x,y}^{\mathcal M_0}(e)\lambda'(e).
\]
\end{theoremv}

\begin{definitionv}{synth_1}[Canonical finite index sets]
For an integer \(n\ge1\), \(\operatorname{Fin}(n)\) denotes the finite index set \(\{0,1,\ldots,n-1\}\). In particular, \(\operatorname{Fin}(2)=\{0,1\}\) and \(\operatorname{Fin}(3)=\{0,1,2\}\), used as finite state spaces with cardinalities \(|\operatorname{Fin}(2)|=2\) and \(|\operatorname{Fin}(3)|=3\).
\end{definitionv}

\begin{propositionv}{prop:strict-fullrank-extension}[Strict rank extension]
For any normalized finite latent-shift SCM \(\mathcal M\) on finite state spaces \(\mathcal E,\mathcal U,\mathcal W,\mathcal X,\mathcal Y\), with \(\mathcal M\in\mathfrak M_{+}\) as in \cref{obj:def:positive-latent-shift-class}, the following implication holds for every treatment \(x\in\mathcal X\): if
\[
\operatorname{rank}(B_x)=|\mathcal U|,
\]
then
\[
\{v\in\mathbb R^{\mathcal W}:\exists \lambda\in\mathbb R^{\mathcal E}\text{ with }B_x\lambda=v\}
=
\{v\in\mathbb R^{\mathcal W}:\exists q\in\mathbb R^{\mathcal U}\text{ with }Mq=v\}
\]
and the balancing fiber \(\Lambda_x(\mathcal D)=\{\lambda\in\mathbb R^{\mathcal E}:B_x\lambda=b\}\) from \cref{obj:def:balancing-fiber} is nonempty.

Moreover, the explicit construction \(\mathcal M^{\star}\) in \cref{obj:def:rank-deficient-success-witness} satisfies all of the following:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Positive class.)} \(\mathcal M^{\star}\in\mathfrak M_{+}\).
\item \textbf{(Treatment-wise rank.)} For every \(x\in\operatorname{Fin}(2)\), \(\operatorname{rank}(B_x)=2\).
\item \textbf{(Treatment-wise target span.)} For every \(x\in\operatorname{Fin}(2)\), \(\Lambda_x(\mathcal D)=\{\lambda\in\mathbb R^{\operatorname{Fin}(2)}:B_x\lambda=b\}\) is nonempty.
\item \textbf{(Strict latent cardinality.)} \(2<|\operatorname{Fin}(3)|\).
\end{itemize}
\end{propositionv}

\begin{theoremv}{thm:finite-sample-projection-coverage}[Finite-sample projection coverage]
Let \(\mathcal M\) be a latent-shift SCM on finite state spaces
\(\mathcal E,\mathcal U,\mathcal W,\mathcal X,\mathcal Y\), let \(P_O\) be an observed source law, and let \(b\) be a target proxy law. Fix \(x\in\mathcal X\) and \(y\in\mathcal Y\). Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Positive latent shift.)} \(\mathcal M\in\mathfrak M_{+}\) in the sense of \cref{obj:def:positive-latent-shift-class}.
\item \textbf{(Compatibility.)} \(\mathcal M\in\mathfrak F(\mathcal D)\), with \(\mathcal D=(P_O,b)\), in the sense of \cref{obj:def:compatible-fiber}.
\item \textbf{(Balancing feasibility.)} The affine balancing set \(\Lambda_x(\mathcal D)\) from \cref{obj:def:balancing-fiber} is nonempty; equivalently, there exists \(\lambda:\mathcal E\to\mathbb R\) such that \(B_x\lambda=b\).
\item \textbf{(Sample sizes and level.)} The sample sizes satisfy \(n_s>0\) and \(n_t>0\), and the nominal error level satisfies \(0<\alpha<1\).
\end{itemize}
Define the two-sample product law by
\[
\mathbb P_{\mathcal M}^{\,n_s,n_t}
=
P_O^{\otimes n_s}\otimes b^{\otimes n_t}.
\]
Then
\[
1-\alpha
\le
\mathbb P_{\mathcal M}^{\,n_s,n_t}
\left\{
\sum_{u\in\mathcal U}\sum_{w\in\mathcal W}
q(u)M(w,u)f_{x,y}(u,w)
\in
\widehat C_{x,y,1-\alpha}
\right\},
\]
where \(\widehat C_{x,y,1-\alpha}\) is the concentration-calibrated projection set of \cref{obj:def:concentration-projection-set} formed from \(\widehat H_x\), \(\widehat z_{x,y}\), \(\widehat b\), \(n_s\), \(n_t\), and \(\alpha\).
\end{theoremv}

\begin{theoremv}{thm:no-uniform-studentized-wald-adaptation}[Wald adaptation separation]
Fix a source allocation limit \(p\in(0,1)\), an error level \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), and deterministic allocation sequences \(n_s(n)\) and \(n_t(n)\) satisfying \cref{obj:ass:triangular-allocation}. For each \(n\ge2\), write \(\Omega_n=\Omega(n_s(n),n_t(n))\), and for any triangular array \(\mathbb M=(\mathcal M_n)_{n\ge2}\) define the row-\(n\) target interventional probability by
\[
\theta_{0,1,n}(\mathcal M_n)
=
\sum_{u,w} q_n(u)M_n(w\mid u)f_{0,1,n}(u,w).
\]
Then there exist a fixed latent-shift SCM \(\mathcal M^{(0)}\) with \(\mathcal E=\mathcal U=\mathcal W=\mathcal Y=\{0,1\}\) and singleton treatment space \(\mathcal X=\{0\}\), and a two-sample triangular array \(\mathbb M^{(1)}=(\mathcal M^{(1)}_n)_{n\ge2}\) on the same state spaces and allocation sequences, such that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Regular baseline.)} \(\mathcal M^{(0)}\in\mathcal R_{1,1/4,1/16}\) for treatment \(0\), outcome \(1\), and source allocation limit \(p\).
\item \textbf{(Array class.)} \(\mathbb M^{(1)}\in\mathcal A_p\) for treatment \(0\) and the allocation sequences \(n_s,n_t\).
\item \textbf{(Separated targets.)} The baseline and row targets satisfy
\[
\theta_{0,1}(\mathcal M^{(0)})=\frac12,
\qquad
\theta_{0,1,n}(\mathcal M^{(1)}_n)=\frac58
\quad\text{for every } n\ge2 .
\]
\item \textbf{(Contiguous row laws.)} The row laws induced by \(\mathbb M^{(1)}\) and by repeating \(\mathcal M^{(0)}\) along the same allocation sequence satisfy
\[
d_{\mathrm{TV}}\!\left(
\mathbb P_{\mathcal M^{(1)}_n}^{\,n_s(n),n_t(n)},
\mathbb P_{\mathcal M^{(0)}}^{\,n_s(n),n_t(n)}
\right)\longrightarrow 0 .
\]
\end{itemize}
Consequently, for every confidence-set sequence \((\mathcal C_n)_{n\ge2}\), with each reported set nonempty and contained in \([0,1]\), satisfying the uniform array coverage condition
\[
1-\alpha
\le
\liminf_{n\to\infty}
\inf_{\mathbb M\in\mathcal A_p}
\mathbb P_{\mathcal M_n}^{\,n_s(n),n_t(n)}
\!\left\{
\theta_{0,1,n}(\mathcal M_n)\in\mathcal C_n
\right\},
\]
and for every Wald-localization slack \(\varepsilon\in(0,1/8)\), the rank-one Wald interval \(I^W_{n,1-\alpha}(\omega)\) computed at \(\mathcal M^{(0)}\), treatment \(0\), outcome \(1\), source allocation limit \(p\), allocation sequences \(n_s,n_t\), and nominal level \(\alpha\) satisfies
\[
1-\alpha
\le
\liminf_{n\to\infty}
\mathbb P_{\mathcal M^{(0)}}^{\,n_s(n),n_t(n)}
\!\left\{
I^W_{n,1-\alpha}\ne\varnothing,\ 
\frac18-\varepsilon
\le
d_H\!\left(\mathcal C_n(\omega),I^W_{n,1-\alpha}(\omega)\right)
\right\}.
\]
\end{theoremv}
